_comment: LBNL FDD Fan-Power Unit (FPU; parallel PFPU / series SFPU) point -> CAMBER Role mapping. Faults are imposed in the SOUTH zone (column suffix _S): diffing each faulted run against PFPU_FaultFree shows the changed columns are RH_*_S / VAV_*_S, so the _S box is the device under test (the _E/_I/_W zones stay healthy; until 0.82.0 this mapping pointed at _W and scored a healthy box). The reheat valve is the controller DEMAND (RH_VLV_DM_S), not the measured position: the drift detector reads how far the controller has to open the valve, and a stuck or leaking valve's position is exactly what the controller cannot see. 0.98 (#85): the measured position RH_VLV_S is mapped as well, to heat_valve_position. heat_valve stays the demand, so the drift detector, reheat_capacity_shortfall and overcooling_severity (which ask how hard the controller calls for heat) are unchanged; reheat_penalty and overcooling_min_flow judge the heat actually delivered and read the position when it is mapped. Evidence: RH_VLV_S equals RH_VLV_DM_S in the healthy runs (correlation 1.0, mean absolute difference 0.0001-0.0002 on the 0-1 scale in PFPU_FaultFree, VAVDMPRStuck_100% and ReheatVLVLeak_50%MaxFlow) and is a constant 0 in ReheatVLVStuck_0%, where the demand is at or above 0.9 in 16% of all minutes. VAV_DMPR_S has no demand twin in this dataset, so it is the position. The reheat dT for the reheat-valve detector is VAV_DAT_S (leaving, warm) minus the AHU supply SA_TEMP (entering the box, cool): SA_TEMP maps to mixed_air_temp, CAMBER's role for a terminal's entering primary air, and is a PROXY for the coil's entering air (in a parallel box the fan adds plenum air when it runs). The room setpoints RMCLGSPT_S / RMHTGSPT_S map to cool_sp / heat_sp (added in 0.86.0; without them unmet_setpoint_hours never evaluated). Timestamps are month-first and the catalog pins the format. Dataset: LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets (CC-BY).
